market_holds: Spot $28.44 (sealed 18:08 UTC). Options price an event move of 8.24% (front-expiry straddle 8.97%, ATM IV 107%), more than twice the 3.62% median of the last 8 reactions, and 25-delta skew of +7.6 vol points means downside is paid for (sealed baseline). The run-in is negative: -15.3% over 20 days and -19.8% from the 52-week high. That drawdown ties to dated news: -6.9% on 2026-10-09, the day after IDC's Q3 tracker showed HP PC units -30.9%, and -9.6% on 2026-10-30 after Intel called PC units -12% for 2026 and -10% for 2027 (Yahoo daily bars; StockStory 2026-10-30). Consensus on Yahoo, 2026-11-24: Q4 non-GAAP EPS $0.741 (13 analysts, up from $0.668 90 days ago, unchanged over 30 days) on revenue of $15.30B. That sits on the $0.74 midpoint of the $0.69-0.79 guide, which includes $0.08 of tariff refunds. Q1 FY27 is $0.711. FY27 is $3.147 (range $2.75-3.54, 18 analysts), essentially flat over 30 days ($3.154) after rising from $2.996 90 days ago. FY26 is $3.237, which includes $0.19 of tariff refunds. Short interest is 76.4M shares, 9.9% of float, as of 2026-10-30, up from 73.1M (about 5.7 days of volume). The mean target of $27.55 is below spot, with a Hold consensus. The stock trades on the FY27 EPS guide, which the CFO promised for this call. Last year the FY guide came in below consensus and the stock slid.
view: This print is decided by the first FY27 guide, given by an interim CEO six weeks before a new CEO (Emma Walmsley, 8-K of 2026-11-04) starts on 2027-01-04. The sell-side FY27 number of $3.15 did not move after the three datapoints that hit the stock in October and November: IDC's HP -30.9% units (Oct 8), Intel's call of 2027 PC units -10% (Oct 29), which is roughly double HP's own 8-K planning assumption of a mid-single-digit decline, and TrendForce's +13-18% PC DRAM in Q4 with further gradual rises into 2027. On the guide's own arithmetic, $3.15 means underlying growth from about $3.05 in FY26 once the non-recurring $0.19 of tariff refunds is removed. It also means a full year of high-cost memory, where FY26 H1 still had cheap strategic inventory. A board handing over to a new CEO has reason to guide in a beatable way. So I think a guide midpoint at or below consensus is more likely than not, and Q4 revenue carries some miss risk: HP said H2 units would fall high teens, while IDC measured -31% for HP in Jul-Sep. Against that, the price has already moved on exactly this news. The stock is down 20% to about 9x FY27, 9.9% of the float is short and rising, skew pays for downside, and options imply 8%. HP has beaten its EPS guide range every quarter in FY26. The CFO said she has 'high confidence' PS margins improve from the Q4 trough, and on that framework (PS margin averaging about 4.3-4.5%, Print 17-18%) $3.15 is reachable, so consensus is not clearly wrong. Lenovo's Jul-Sep quarter showed pricing pass-through working, with devices revenue +15% on units down about 22%. Dell reports the same evening and adds noise I cannot forecast. Net: I lean slightly to a lower open, but not enough to bet on.
unpriced: The FY27 sell-side number ($3.147) has not been revised for Intel's -10% 2027 PC call, IDC's -31% HP units or the continued DRAM increases. It is a stale estimate, and a guide below it is somewhat more likely than the consensus implies. But the price has already fallen on each of those datapoints, and 9.9% of the float is short, so I cannot show that the price, as opposed to the estimate, fails to hold it. No recommendation.

recommendation.reason: The FY27 consensus is stale against October's PC and memory data and the CEO transition favours a cautious guide, so the tilt is down. But the stock already fell about 20% on that same data, short interest is 9.9% and rising, skew already pays for downside, and HP has beaten its EPS guide each quarter. The gap between the estimate and the price is not shown to be in the price's disfavour by enough to clear 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A FY27 non-GAAP EPS guide with a midpoint at or above about $3.15, together with a statement that memory costs peak in FY26 Q4, would likely squeeze a crowded short up. A midpoint near $2.90 or below, or a deferred or partial guide because of the CEO change, would make the down case.

self_critique: The strongest case against a down tilt: every bearish datapoint is dated and already produced a tradeable drop. At about 9x FY27, with 10% of the float short and a mean target barely below spot, the buy-side bar is probably well under the $3.15 sell-side figure. HP's management has repeatedly guided conservatively and then beaten, and promised margin recovery with 'high confidence', so a guide near $3.0-3.2 with buyback support could squeeze the stock up. Dell's same-night results add noise in either direction. The case for a bigger down tilt: Intel's -10% 2027 view, plus no tariff refunds and a full year of high-cost memory, makes a guide midpoint near $2.8-2.9 plausible, which would be a 7-10% gap to consensus.
approach_notes: P4 (prove 'priced in') helped by splitting the estimate (stale) from the price (moved), which is what kept this at no-call. P6 positioning was useful. A rule for the case where estimates are stale but the price has already moved on the same datapoints would help.
